These hypotheses come from what is known about NAS-Bench-201 rather than from a fresh query of the benchmark. They rely on four regularities:

- **Disconnection is catastrophic.** If a cell has no live path from input to output (node 0 to node 3), accuracy collapses to about chance. So removing an edge hurts much more when it is the last remaining path.
- **Edges into the output are critical.** Edges 3, 4 and 5 carry everything that reaches node 3, so their redundancy decides how damaging an edit is.
- **Convolutions matter most where computation is missing.** A 3×3 convolution adds the most when it fills an empty (none) or weak (pooling-only) slot.
- **Residual cells need a convolution path.** A skip connection on edge 3 is most useful when there is a deep convolutional path for it to bypass.
